$comment: DECLARED ALLOW-LIST of VITE_* variables permitted in the built client bundle.
Every variable here is readable by ANYONE who loads the site. `VITE_` is not a
scope — it is a publication instruction to Vite. Before adding an entry, answer:
is this a credential? If yes it must not be VITE_-prefixed at all; move it
Feature-flag keys are NOT listed here — they are derived from src/lib/flagEnv.ts
at check time, so adding a flag never requires touching this file. This list is
only the NON-flag variables, and it is deliberately a hand-maintained mirror:
it is safe to be one because the guard FAILS LOUD on anything absent from it,
forcing a human to classify a new variable rather than letting it appear silently.

notes.VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: Public by design — Supabase anon keys are meant to reach the browser; user data is protected by RLS, not by hiding this.
notes.VITE_SENTRY_DSN: Public by design — a Sentry DSN is an ingest endpoint, not a secret.

VITE_PLOT_BEARER.reason: A SHARED SERVER-TO-SERVER CREDENTIAL (PLoT's PLOT_AUTH_TOKEN, also used by CEE) shipped to the browser by a ratified POC decision. Narrowing removed its NAME from the bundle but its VALUE is still inlined once, in the plotAuthHeaders chunk, because the browser genuinely needs it until the same-origin proxy lands. Removing it before the proxy is a staging outage for every PLoT-direct seam. See SECURITY-PLOT-BEARER-2026-07-28.md sections 6 and 7; rotation is sequenced AFTER the proxy.

knownExposed.VITE_ACCESS_CODES: Credential-shaped name read by src/lib/auth/accessValidation.ts. Not present in the measured build (unset), so not currently exposed — listed here so that setting it is a loud event rather than a silent one.
knownExposed.VITE_ACCESS_SALT: As above — a salt in a client bundle provides no secrecy. Review before this is ever set.
knownExposed.VITE_POSTHOG_KEY: PostHog project keys are write-only and intended to be public, but the name is credential-shaped; kept visible here deliberately. ROADMAP 2.111: this is now the ONLY PostHog key name in the repo — the former second name VITE_POSTHOG_API_KEY was removed (not aliased) so activation cannot leave one consumer dark.
knownExposed.VITE_POSTHOG_HOST: Public endpoint; grouped with the PostHog key for review.
knownExposed.VITE_STORAGE_KEY: Read by src/lib/secureStorage.ts. A client-side encryption key in the bundle is not a secret from the user; review what it is protecting.
knownExposed.VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY: Was baked as the literal "placeholder" before this change and is no longer in the bundle. If a REAL key is ever set here it would be published to every visitor; the guard will red on it.
